Routing metrics are now copy-on-write.
Initially a route entry points it's metrics at a read-only location.
If a routing table entry exists
column2: it will point there.  Else it will

column1: point at the all zero metric place-holder called 'dst_default_metrics'.
The writeability state of the metrics is stored in the low bits of the
metrics pointer
column2: we have two bits left to spare if we want to store

column1: more states.
For the initial implementation
column2: COW is implemented simply via kmalloc.

column1: However future enhancements will change this to place the writable
metrics somewhere else
column2: in order to increase sharing.  Very likely

column1: this ""somewhere else"" will be the inetpeer cache.
Note also that this means that metrics updates may transiently fail
if we cannot COW the metrics successfully.
But even by itself
column2: this patch should decrease memory usage and

column1: increase cache locality especially for routing workloads.  In those
cases the read-only metric copies stay in place and never get written
to.
TCP workloads where metrics get updated
PMTU triggers occur
column2: will take a very slight performance hit.  But

column1: that hit will be alleviated when the long-term writable metrics
move to a more sharable location.
Since the metrics storage went from a u32 array of RTAX_MAX entries to
what is essentially a pointer
column2: some retooling of the dst_entry layout

column1: was necessary.
Most importantly
column2: we need to preserve the alignment of the reference

column1: count so that it doesn't share cache lines with the read-mostly state
as per Eric Dumazet's alignment assertion checks.
The only non-trivial bit here is the move of the 'flags' member into
the writeable cacheline.  This is OK since we are always accessing the
flags around the same moment when we made a modification to the
reference count.
